scope: Finite independent source and retained CPU-test review; not an actual archive, prune, offload, restore, or NTFS durability qualification.

author_tests.reason: Final source/test delta and exact retained test evidence reviewed; no duplicate test campaign requested.

resolved_finding.problem: Canonical destination path alone did not bind offload to the original external filesystem.
resolved_finding.resolution: Before offload marker/output creation, destination parent device equals the archived source root device and differs from held local archive device; local release independently checks held remote device against original source and local archive before release marker/unlink.
regressions: Wrong-filesystem offload refuses before marker/create while retaining archive
Identical rebound remote payload and rewritten receipt on wrong device refuses before local-release marker/unlink

reviewed_guards: Fixed closed baseline authority and exact 27-way partition; only indexed regular .bin files are removable
All archive members, sizes and SHA256 values verified before pruning, with full archive identity/hash retained
Held no-follow source root/parent traversal; per-file original hash and identity checked immediately before unlink
Durable pre-prune incomplete marker and exact archive-relative restore map; no automatic retry
Six micro input/output files retained and rehashed; JSON, logs, directories, models and candidate run excluded
Held archive and path identity checked before every source unlink
External full-copy readback and complete member reverification before local archive removal
Compressed archive/stat budget 384MiB and 27GB plus64MiB floor; previous batch release required before next batch
limitations: No hostile concurrent same-user mutation guarantee; checks detect ordinary identity/metadata/hash changes but are not an atomic filesystem snapshot.
Directory fsync failure immediately after unlink can leave progress counter one file behind; durable full restore map and verified archive remain, and success is refused.
Tiny cross-filesystem CPU tests do not establish durability of the actual NTFS mount; root owns actual phase execution and filesystem evidence.
Archive stores exact bytes and per-file stat metadata; recovery requires separately reviewed restoration of missing paths, with no automatic overwrite.
